gen-dafont-bloody-fs-fira-sans: Round, swollen lowercase bowls give Bloody its menace. Fira Sans steps in with a wide-open, large-x-height body, and the two hold together because one shouts while the other simply speaks.
gen-dafont-origami-work-sans: Origami looks like single brush strokes of constant width, stacked into a lowercase mass as dense as poured lead type. And Work Sans, with its high mean line and open c tips, keeps a long paragraph moving without any strain.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-switzer: Outrun Future spreads its letters wide and draws them as a constant-width outline you could trace with a finger. But Switzer's wire-like forms stay approachable, so give that body text a little extra size.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-switzer: Stretched out and cheeky, Early GameBoy spaces its letters wide and shows a modest swing between thick and thin strokes. It loves to announce; Switzer prefers to explain.
gen-dafont-joystix-switzer: Bold and arcade-minded, Joystix tracks its letters far apart, with stems barely heavier than the arms joining them. Switzer's wire-bent lines make the quiet partner.
gen-gf-offside-archivo: Offside's curves refuse to close, and its widely spaced letters keep a level, accent-free beat. Archivo takes over below with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height.
gen-dafont-quantum-fs-fira-sans: Quantum lets its letters breathe, with loose fit and mouths that stay open, while its ascenders are cut short. Fira Sans follows with a larger x-height and no stroke contrast.
gen-dafont-woodgod-satoshi: Commanding and vintage, Woodgod pairs a wide channel into every bowl with lowercase that nearly reaches its capitals. Satoshi then settles in beneath, its soaring x-height and open e reading like a ballpoint line.
gen-gf-metamorphous-fs-public-sans: Wide sidebearings and a high midline give Metamorphous a stately, spaced-out look. And Public Sans, hefty and open on c and s, carries a long paragraph without tiring the eye.
gen-gf-oxanium-fs-supreme: A high x-height makes Oxanium's lowercase look big, drawn in uninterrupted monoline strokes. Supreme follows with a heavy-looking band of text that holds its curves open, so a long paragraph stays crisp.
